name: TensorPM v1.38.1
body:
# Changelog - v1.38.1

This update expands browser-assisted project work, improves document editing and AI change review,
and makes incoming project information easier to inspect. It includes all changes since v1.38.0.

## 🎉 New Features

### Browse Websites Directly Inside TensorPM

A new integrated browser brings websites into the project workspace. Open pages yourself, keep
multiple tabs, and assign a task on an existing page to the Browser Agent.

- Work with the browser beside your project conversation, resize its dock or expand it to full width.
- Minimize the browser to a Pulse card and reopen it without losing the current page.
- Use familiar navigation controls, an address bar, browsing history, page search and zoom.
- Access page printing, screenshots and device-width previews from the browser controls.
- Keep browser tabs available after an agent task ends, including pages you opened yourself.
- View desktop layouts even in a narrow dock; the display scales with the available space.

The Browser Agent now uses TensorPM's integrated browser. Setup no longer requires a separate
Chromium download; Browser-Use and its Python requirements remain managed through Settings.

### Share Browser Control with the Agent

Watch the agent's progress, take control to complete a login or another manual step, and return
control when you are ready. The same page and its entered values remain available across handovers.

- Give follow-up instructions or stop the task from its browser controls.
- Respond to the agent's requests for information or manual assistance within the browser workspace.
- Enable individual approvals for browser actions when you want to review them before execution.
- Give the task specific success criteria, allowed websites and selected project files.
- Keep independent browser tasks and tabs isolated so one task cannot take over another task's page.

### More Useful Browser Results and Downloads

Browser tasks now distinguish completed work from partial, blocked, failed or cancelled outcomes.
The agent checks the requested outcome and retains the findings and uncertainties collected along
the way.

- A short completion notice is followed by a consolidated Project Agent answer based on the full results.
- Long results can be read in pages without losing the continuation information.
- Downloaded and generated files are registered with the project and linked to the task's results.
- Task results and pending completion notices survive an application restart.
- Interrupted tasks are retained for inspection and require an explicit new start before continuing work.

### GPT-6 Astra in the Model Selector

GPT-6 Astra is available in the OpenAI model selector, including image input support and its configured
context and output limits. The selected model is preserved when you reload the application.

### Read Source Previews Before Distilling

Hover over an incoming email, document, supported local file or Telegram message to read a longer
preview before deciding what to distill.

- Email previews show the available message body instead of only the short queue excerpt.
- Supported local files include text, Markdown, CSV, spreadsheets, Word documents, presentations and PDFs.
- Previews clearly indicate when long content has been shortened.
- Private-source previews respect the source's project and viewer access.
- Opening a preview leaves the source's intake status unchanged and does not start an AI request.
- File extraction runs separately from the main application, with time and size limits to keep the interface responsive.

## 📝 Artifact Mode Improvements

### Keep or Undo Individual AI Changes

Review one AI change at a time, or keep or undo the remaining changes from the same turn together.
This works for text, formatting, diagrams and text boxes, with visible notices for deleted text blocks.

- Accepting one change leaves the other changes available for review.
- Pending review marks, deletion positions and undo/redo history survive closing and reopening a document.
- Undoing remaining changes preserves changes you already accepted.
- Deleted text boxes are restored by the combined undo action, including after reopening the document.
- Selective undo restores neighboring deleted blocks in their correct order and respects retained moves.

### Easier Diagram and Text-Box Editing

- Select diagrams directly on the page, move them with a drag handle or remove them with the delete control.
- Backspace and Delete operate on the selected diagram; selection receives keyboard focus immediately.
- Moving a diagram preserves its identity, source, width and alignment, including across undo and redo.
- Enter text boxes by mouse or keyboard and apply formatting through the shared document toolbar.
- Text-box toolbar changes save reliably, even when focus temporarily moves to a formatting control.
- Delayed save acknowledgements preserve newer typing, and undo/redo updates the focused text box correctly.

### More Reliable Document-Agent Work

- The ChatGPT/Codex subscription provider can access TensorPM's document tools through its app-server integration.
- Long reading sessions can summarize earlier reading progress and continue within the same request.
- After reading history is summarized, the agent must read content again before editing it or quoting it exactly.
- Completed edits retain their tool receipts when Stop is pressed during a layout update.
- Cancellation and revision checks protect against applying stale results after asynchronous work.

### More Accurate Layout Updates

AI changes to heading and paragraph spacing appear immediately on the page. Review markers no longer
interfere with pagination measurements, and diagram controls remain hidden in printed output.
Text-box formatting menus preserve the active editing context.

## 🔎 Clearer Distiller and Trail Views

Long text changes now open in a clean reading view. Expand the full text, show the previous version
or turn on change highlighting when you need a detailed comparison.

- Text previews prefer complete paragraphs or sentences where possible.
- Collapsed descriptions stay within their cards and no longer overlap the expansion control or reasoning.
- Table comparisons use thin, aligned cell borders with consistent old/new rows.
- Narrow cards keep action labels and controls inside the available width.
- Requirement priority charts use consistent colors across supported priority labels and legends.

## 💬 Project-Agent and Workflow Improvements

- Direct chat replies follow the language of the current user message, while new or edited project
  content follows the configured application language.
- German project-management instructions use consistent terminology, including Aufgaben, Aufwand,
  Projektstrukturplan and kritischer Pfad, and distinguish estimates from confirmed commitments.
- Completed browser tasks no longer inject their old task instructions into unrelated later messages.
- Tool guidance for sandbox document generation stays aligned with the bundled libraries and their versions.
- Project navigation retains the selected sidebar tab during rapid tab changes.

## 🐛 Additional Fixes and Security

- Wizard table edits and row removal use stable row identities. Sorting, filtering or deleting a row
  no longer redirects a delayed edit into another row.
- Embedded browser content stays beneath dialogs and disappears when its host is hidden or clipped.
- Background browser views are genuinely hidden. Preview capture, viewport updates and control
  handovers are coordinated so stale rendering work cannot flash a browser surface over the app.
- Browser control transitions preserve keyboard input and page state, and late updates cannot revive a finished task.
- Browser startup and stop handling clean up failed or interrupted processes more reliably.
- HTML in chat messages cannot inject page metadata that redirects or repeatedly reloads the app.
- Malformed image containers are rejected promptly instead of potentially leaving image processing stuck.

## 🛠️ Maintenance and Quality Checks

- Windows release signing now covers the application, bundled executables, native DLLs and addons,
  elevation helper and uninstaller, as well as the final Setup and AppX packages.
- Windows release checks verify signatures and timestamps, compare installed binaries with the
  verified payload, and scan release files with Microsoft Defender before publication. Signing and
  scan reports are retained with the build. AppX and updater publisher identities use the certificate's
  full subject name.
- Updated OpenAI/Codex, Anthropic, Google, PowerSync and email dependencies.
- Aligned TipTap editor packages for reproducible clean installations and grouped future updates
  across runtime and development dependencies to avoid incompatible partial upgrades.
- Expanded real Electron coverage for document review, diagram editing, browser handovers, source previews,
  responsive layouts and project navigation.
- Added browser-task checks for approvals, outcomes, process lifecycle, restart recovery and downloaded files.
- Isolated Electron test data per run and worker, and made renderer exceptions and unhandled rejections visible as test failures.
- Kept live-provider tests separate from the deterministic unit and integration suites.
